pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/mcp/route.ts:273 The dispatch door now resolves handlers through one registry (the stale 'separate switch' verdict is fixed: tool-registry.ts plus a pinning test), but it still runs every handler with no door-level wall-clock budget and returns its result with no door-level size cap, so one slow or oversized handler is bounded only by its own discipline.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/mcp/route.ts:273 Registry, dispatch and the fault catch (route.ts:318) are one spine now. But the technique makes timeouts and result-size caps door policy, and the route applies neither around runTool or toolResultText. Athena caps results at 12_000 chars; the MCP door does not.

src/lib/mcp/tools.ts:493 Validation is right: the validator reads the published inputSchema (handlers.ts:443) and failures go in-band (handlers.ts:447). The gap is that the wire shape publishes no read-only/destructive/idempotent hints, and the server-side `mutates?: true` is optional, so an absent hint stands in for a verdict.
src/app/api/mcp/route.ts:293 The audit row, WRITE_TOOL_POLICY and the bindings are all keyed on the addressable name. No rename-stable identifier is published on the definition or on the result.

src/app/api/mcp/route.ts:238 Per-token bearer auth, verified before any argument handling (route.ts:119). Scopes come from the existing org API-token registry. Audit actor, rate limit and holder key on the minted token id, not its name, and revocation is a revokedAt path.
src/app/api/mcp/route.ts:101 Streamable-HTTP door with origin validation on by default, failing closed when no site URL is set, plus a mandatory bearer token on every request.
src/app/api/mcp/route.ts:308 Org-authored results get credential shapes redacted and a provenance _meta stamped before serialization. This is keyed on the catalog's required resultTrust field.
src/lib/mcp/handlers.ts:137 Every listing takes an org that the route derives from the verified token (token.orgSlug). No caller-supplied org exists, so no listing lacks a scope.
src/lib/mcp/tools.ts:488 A 16-tool catalog, filtered by scope, sits far below any host's hard tool ceiling, so there is no projection pressure.
src/app/api/mcp/route.ts:7 Stateless, with no affinity requirement.
src/app/api/mcp/route.ts:177 No elicitation or suspension exists. Listing is a pure function of the token's scopes and the plan gates.

pairs.registryProposal: tool-identity-vs-tool-name should state whether its precondition is 'a catalog that has renamed or will rename' or 'any published catalog'. A small catalog that has never renamed a tool reads as either not-applicable or a deviation, depending on the seat.

pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: src/lib/athena/grounding.ts:141 Athena's tool set is still the whole MCP catalog minus writes, minus holder-bound bindings, minus closed plan gates. She is not admitted by an explicit scope grant through the protocol door's own toolsForScopes, so a future read tool behind a scope no token of hers carries would be offered to every org member by default.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/athena/grounding.ts:141 Admission by exclusion, which the technique names as the failure shape. There is no scope grant and no shared admission with route.ts toolsForScopes.
src/lib/athena/grounding.ts:228 Org-authored results are redacted and fenced as untrusted data before the model reads them.
src/lib/athena/grounding.ts:219 Uses the same dispatcher (runTool via the registry) and the same serializer as the MCP door, so both doors show byte-identical text.
src/lib/athena/grounding.ts:183 Write tools are subtracted by name, and the refusal names this surface and its reason.

declined.subject: mcp-tools
declined.reason: Its listed files (page.tsx, ScanForm.tsx, src/app/api/scan/**) contain no MCP vocabulary. But its directories include src/app and src/components, which also hold the MCP door (src/app/api/mcp), so an absence claimed by directory search would be refused, and nothing in the context positively shows applicability.
